entities.name: Serenus of Antinouplis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Serenus of Antinoöpolis, a Greek mathematician flourishing in the Late Antique Thebaid of Roman Egypt, likely in the late 4th century CE, stands as a crucial figure in the transmission of Hellenistic geometric knowledge. Operating within the intellectual orbit of the declining Alexandrian school, Serenus dedicated his work to the rigorous study of conic and cylindrical sections, contributing to a tradition stretching back to Euclid and Apollonius. His treatises, though highly specialized, reflect a commitment to preserving and clarifying complex mathematical principles during an era when such scholarship was increasingly rare.

His two principal extant works are *On the Section of a Cylinder* and *On the Section of a Cone*. In the former, Serenus meticulously demonstrates that all sections of an oblique cylinder made by planes parallel to its axis are ellipses, a nuanced geometric insight. The latter treatise, *On the Section of a Cone*, aimed to prove that the conic sections studied by Apollonius of Perga are identical to those formed by cutting a cone with a plane. This work was explicitly intended to preface Apollonius's monumental *Conics*, suggesting Serenus saw his role as clarifying and validating the foundations of earlier, more complex works for his contemporaries.

Serenus's enduring legacy lies primarily in his role as a conservator and expositor of sophisticated Greek mathematics. His writings were incorporated into the mathematical curriculum of Late Antiquity and were studied by later scholars, including Pappus of Alexandria, who might have been a contemporary or slightly earlier figure, indicating a shared intellectual milieu. By meticulously re-examining and proving fundamental geometric theorems, Serenus ensured that the intricate knowledge of conic sections, so vital to astronomy and engineering, remained accessible and understood as the classical world transitioned into the early medieval period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Serenus of Antinoöpolis played a significant role in preserving and clarifying advanced Greek geometric knowledge during Late Antiquity, particularly through his treatises on conic and cylindrical sections. His work helped ensure the transmission of these complex mathematical concepts to later Byzantine and Islamic scholarship, preventing their complete loss.
